subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Islam: Beliefs, Crime & Punishment, Living the Muslim Life, Peace & Conflict (Spec A)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the term Tawhid mean?
options: The oneness and unity of Allah
questions.explain: Tawhid is the central Muslim belief in the absolute oneness and unity of Allah.

questions.q: In Islam, Muhammad is described as the 'Seal of the Prophets'. What does this mean?
options: He was the last and final prophet sent by Allah
He was the first prophet Allah created
He was the only prophet in Islam
questions.explain: As the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad is believed to be the final messenger, completing Allah's revelation.

questions.q: What does the Arabic term akhirah refer to?
questions.explain: Akhirah is the Muslim belief in everlasting life after death, including judgement, heaven and hell.

questions.q: According to Muslim belief, which holy book was revealed to the prophet Musa (Moses)?
questions.explain: Muslims believe the Tawrat was revealed to Musa, while the Injil was given to Isa and the Zabur to Dawud.

questions.q: Belief in predestination (al-Qadr) is one of the Six Beliefs of Sunni Islam. What does it teach?
options: Allah already knows and has decreed all that will happen
Humans have no soul after death
questions.explain: Al-Qadr is the belief that Allah, in his supreme will and knowledge, has determined everything that happens.

questions.q: What is meant by risalah in Islam?
options: The channel of prophethood through which Allah communicates
The obligation to give money to charity
The struggle against evil in oneself
questions.explain: Risalah refers to the messengership or prophethood through which Allah sends guidance to humanity.

questions.q: In Muslim belief, what role did the angel Jibril (Gabriel) play?
options: He revealed the words of the Qur'an to Muhammad
He records people's good and bad deeds
He takes away souls at death
He blows the trumpet on the Day of Judgement
questions.explain: Jibril is the angel who delivered Allah's revelation, the Qur'an, to the Prophet Muhammad.

questions.q: Adalat (divine justice) is one of the Five Roots of Usul ad-Din. To which branch of Islam does this belief especially belong?
questions.explain: Adalat is one of the Five Roots of Usul ad-Din, the key beliefs particularly emphasised in Shia Islam.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists the Five Pillars of Sunni Islam?
options: Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm and Hajj
Tawhid, angels, prophets, books and judgement
Wudu, jihad, khums, imamah and adalat
Ramadan, Eid, Ashura, Hajj and salah
questions.explain: The Five Pillars of Sunni Islam are Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm and Hajj.

questions.q: For Zakah, what proportion of a Muslim's surplus wealth is normally given each year?
questions.explain: Zakah requires eligible Muslims to give 2.5% of their surplus wealth annually to help those in need.

questions.q: During which month of the Islamic calendar do Muslims fast for Sawm?
questions.explain: Sawm is the obligatory fast observed during the daylight hours of the month of Ramadan.

questions.q: In which city does the Hajj pilgrimage take place?
questions.explain: Hajj is the pilgrimage to Makkah, centred on the Ka'aba, which every able Muslim should make once if possible.

questions.q: Khums is one of the Ten Obligatory Acts in Shia Islam. What does it require?
options: Giving 20% of surplus income to religious and charitable causes
Fasting for twenty extra days a year
Making twenty pilgrimages in a lifetime
questions.explain: Khums is a Shia payment of 20% of surplus income, divided between religious leaders and charitable causes.

questions.q: What is the difference between greater jihad and lesser jihad?
options: Greater jihad is the inner spiritual struggle, while lesser jihad is the outward struggle including military defence
Greater jihad is a military war, while lesser jihad is private prayer
Greater jihad is fasting, while lesser jihad is charity
There is no difference between the two
questions.explain: Greater jihad is the personal struggle to live faithfully, whereas lesser jihad refers to the outward, sometimes physical, defence of Islam.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the main aims of punishment studied in Islam?
questions.explain: Deterrence, along with retribution, reformation and protection, is one of the key aims of punishment.

questions.q: What does the aim of punishment known as retribution mean?
options: The criminal should pay for or suffer for the wrong they have done
The criminal should be helped to change and improve
Society should be protected from the criminal
Others should be put off committing the crime
questions.explain: Retribution is the idea that a criminal deserves to be made to pay for the harm they have caused.

questions.q: Why do many Muslims believe forgiveness is important when responding to crime?
options: Allah is merciful and forgiving, so believers should also show mercy
The Qur'an forbids any form of punishment
Forgiveness means criminals never face consequences
Only judges are allowed to forgive
questions.explain: Because Allah is described as the most merciful, many Muslims believe they too should be willing to forgive wrongdoers.

questions.q: Which of the following is a condition commonly required for a war to be considered just in Islam?
options: It must be a last resort, fought in self-defence and not to gain territory
It should be started without warning to gain advantage
It can be waged to force people to convert
questions.explain: Islamic teaching on just war requires conflict to be a last resort, defensive, and never aimed at conquest or harming innocents.

questions.q: What is meant by pacifism?
options: The belief that violence and war are wrong and disputes should be settled peacefully
The belief that war is always necessary
The duty to give money to the poor
questions.explain: Pacifism is the belief that war and violence are unjustifiable and that conflicts should be resolved peacefully.

questions.q: A Muslim carefully calculates 2.5% of their surplus savings and donates it to help the poor. Which pillar are they fulfilling?
questions.explain: Giving 2.5% of surplus wealth to those in need is the pillar of Zakah.

questions.q: A prison runs classes to teach offenders new skills so they can find work and not reoffend after release. Which aim of punishment does this best show?
questions.explain: Helping offenders change their behaviour so they do not reoffend reflects the aim of reformation.

questions.q: After a violent dispute, a Muslim chooses to forgive the person who wronged them and works to rebuild the relationship. Which value are they showing?
questions.explain: Restoring a broken relationship after conflict is an example of reconciliation, valued highly in Islam.

questions.q: A Muslim says that everything that happens is part of Allah's will and knowledge, even before it occurs. Which belief are they expressing?
questions.explain: The belief that Allah knows and has decreed all events reflects al-Qadr, predestination.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Religious Studies A (1RA0) specification; Islam: Beliefs, Crime & Punishment, Living the Muslim Life, Peace & Conflict (Spec A)
